bullets.title: Joe Rogan Experience #1198 - Derren Brown
bullets.note: (**[**Apple Podcasts**](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/27uk8e5mmuoh268p0ar/5gfvh7h0nm9qq9/aHR0cHM6Ly9wb2RjYXN0cy5hcHBsZS5jb20vdXMvcG9kY2FzdC8xMTk4LWRlcnJlbi1icm93bi9pZDM2MDA4NDI3Mj9pPTEwMDA0MjM1NTIzMzY=)**,** [**YouTube**](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/27uk8e5mmuoh268p0ar/55tvh7h0nm9qqz/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cueW91dHViZS5jb20vd2F0Y2g_dj1uX3RwV3J2NzZROA==)**).** I’ve long been fascinated by illusionist and mentalist Derren Brown ([@derrenbrown](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/27uk8e5mmuoh268p0ar/94czhnhx6p200p/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9kZXJyZW5icm93bg==)). But “illusionist and mentalist” doesn’t quite do him justice. Derren’s also an expert in behavioral change, debunking charlatans, portrait painting, and more. In this podcast episode, Joe Rogan ([@joerogan](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/27uk8e5mmuoh268p0ar/n5sohvhgx3ommv/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9Aam9lcm9nYW4=)) does an excellent job of weaving a nearly comprehensive conversation. It takes about 10–15 minutes for them to get really warmed up (as it often does for all long-form podcasts), but then they’re off to the races. Next up on my to-watch list is [Derren Brown: Miracle](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/27uk8e5mmuoh268p0ar/w5a2hgh4kwonnx/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubmV0ZmxpeC5jb20vdGl0bGUvODAyMTk4MDI=).

bullets.section: What I’m wearing to protect against ticks —
bullets.title: ElimiTick Insect Repellent Ultra Lite Pant / TLP
bullets.note: I’ve contracted Lyme disease twice. Lyme seems to be a tax for many people who grew up on Long Island, but I have no desire for a third experience. These ElimiTick pants were gifted to me by a dear friend, and… they really seem to work. I wore them on a recent hike (forgoing tick-repellent spray) and came back with no ticks. The person with me later found more than a dozen ticks on their clothing and skin. Perhaps the chemical coating/treatment will kill me faster than Lyme, but I’ll continue wearing the pants for now. I’ll roll the dice with intermittent permethrin—or whatever they use—instead of rolling the dice with ticks and then downing 200mg of doxycycline as the morning-after pill. Also, for the many people who’ve asked me about recovery from Lyme: (1) I’m not an expert and no MD, but (2) antibiotics plus [a strict ketogenic diet](https://el2.convertkit-mail.com/c/27uk8e5mmuoh268p0ar/pkteh9hd2z7mmo/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYW1hem9uLmNvbS9LZXRvLUNhbmNlci1LZXRvZ2VuaWMtTWV0YWJvbGljLU51dHJpdGlvbmFsLWVib29rLWRwLUIwNzZLRFk4RlIvZHAvQjA3NktEWThGUi9yZWY9bXRfa2luZGxlP19lbmNvZGluZz1VVEY4Jm1lPSZxaWQ9) (but neither alone) seemed to be the key for me, and I’ve since seen that replicated by a few friends. Could be placebo, of course, but I cared more about speed and outcomes, rather than mechanisms.
